chapter: Small groups, Europe and Kansas City memories (repeated passages)
title: Benny Carter's band and his rehearsals
summary: Dickenson enjoyed Benny Carter's band, praises him as musician and arranger, and says he rehearsed bands well and patiently.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: Benny Carter always had good bands, too, didn't he.
Oh yeah. Oh, I enjoyed playing in his band. That was a great band. Of course, it did record.
Yes. On this thing called "My Favorite Blues" he's got a nice solo, Benny, on it.
Yeah, I've got that. I've got all the records... No, not all of them. I ain't got 'em all.
Well, if you're missing any, I think I probably could tape most of them.
[COUGHS[] I don't know if I have "Sleep" or not. I don't think I have.
Oh, I can tape it for you.
Yeah. It's strange that Benny's bands never really seemed to break through in the...
Isn't that... What a great musician he is. I can't say too much when I'm talking about how great a musician he is. He's the greatest with me, you know; one of the greatest. And an arranger...
Yeah... His saxophone sections are always outstanding.
Oh... He rehearses them good. He's a good rehearsal man, too. He sees that you play that thing right.
It seems that he is one of the most respected guys around.
Was he patient? I mean, if there was someone in the band who couldn't really...you know, had a little trouble...
He was patient with them. I told you, he's a good rehearsal man, too. You know?
